## Appearance

Gilbert Blythe is a tall boy with curly brown hair and roguish hazel eyes. His mouth is frequently twisted into a teasing smile.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028)_

## Personality

Gilbert is a clever and good-natured young man who approaches life with a strong determination to both make the most of it and contribute his best. Highly competitive in his studies, he strives to be at the head of his class, while also possessing a playful side that leads him to tease the girls.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 CHAPTER XVII. A New Interest in Life P36](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0036), [v1 CHAPTER XXX. The Queen’s Class Is Organized P24](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0024), [v1 CHAPTER XXXV. The Winter at Queen’s P3](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0003)_

## History

Gilbert Blythe returned to [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) after spending three years in Alberta with his sick father and spending the summer visiting cousins in [New Brunswick](../codex/places.md#new-brunswick). Upon returning to school, he teased [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) by calling her 'Carrots,' which led to her smashing a slate over his head and initiating a bitter, one-sided silence and fierce academic rivalry between them. Despite saving [Anne](../character/anne.md) from a sinking dory on the pond, Gilbert was rebuffed when he attempted to apologize and offer his friendship. The two remained rivals as they tied for first place on the [Island](../codex/places.md#island) on the Queen's [Entrance](../codex/places.md#entrance) examination and went on to attend Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy) together, where Gilbert ultimately won the medal while [Anne](../character/anne.md) earned the Avery scholarship. Upon learning that [Anne](../character/anne.md) planned to stay at [Green Gables](../codex/places.md#green-gables) to care for [Marilla](../character/marilla-cuthbert.md) after Matthew's death, Gilbert generously gave up his accepted teaching position in [Avonlea](../codex/places.md#avonlea) so [Anne](../character/anne.md) could take it. Touched by his sacrifice, [Anne](../character/anne.md) forgave him, and the two finally put an end to their long rivalry and became friends.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P1](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0001), [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P14](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0014), [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P16](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0016), [v1 CHAPTER XV. ## Quotes

> "It wasn’t particularly good of me at all, Anne. I was pleased to be able to do you some small service. Are we going to be friends after this? Have you really forgiven me my old fault?"
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road P52](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0052)

> "We were born to be good friends, Anne. You’ve thwarted destiny enough. I know we can help each other in many ways. You are going to keep up your studies, aren’t you? So am I. Come, I’m going to walk home with you."
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v1 CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road P55](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0055)

> “I’m awfully sorry I made fun of your hair, Anne,” he whispered contritely. “Honest I am. Don’t be mad for keeps, now.”
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P49](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0049)

> "I’ll never ask you to be friends again, Anne Shirley. And I don’t care either!"
>
> — Gilbert Blythe — [v1 CHAPTER XXVIII. An Unfortunate Lily Maid P34](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0034)

> "It was my fault Mr. Phillips. I teased her."

## Relationships

### [Anne](../character/anne.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne--gilbert-blythe.md)

Gilbert's relationship with [Anne](../character/anne.md) began on a rocky note when he pulled her hair and teased her by calling her 'Carrots,' causing her to smash a slate over his head and hold an unforgiving grudge against him. Despite this initial hostility, the two maintain an intense academic rivalry as they compete for the top examination scores in their class. Although some rumors presume a romantic connection between them, [Anne](../character/anne.md) steadfastly maintains her silence toward him.

- Enemy of — unforgiving grudge over insulting teasing  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P51](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0051), [v1 CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot P93](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0093)</sub>

- presumed Romantically involved with  <sub>[v1 CHAPTER XXV. Matthew Insists on Puffed Sleeves P55](../source/v01-c25.md#nw-v01-c25-p0055)</sub>

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--gilbert-blythe.md)

Gilbert faces persistent hatred and contempt from [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) despite his repeated attempts to appease her and apologize. When he rescues her from a sinking dory, she angrily refuses his offer of friendship and apology, maintaining her silent grudge. Nevertheless, their sharp academic rivalry pushes them both to excel, and his presence even fuels her pride to overcome stage fright during a major recitative performance.
